items.note: Larrow Valley Cooperative Creamery Association, 1889, Gideon Vose president 1889-1911, creamery at Larrow Green 1891.
Article VII: paid on pounds of butterfat by test, 'the test of the station where he delivers shall govern', contrasted with payment by weight.
'Under payment by weight, nothing that happened later would have cost anyone a dollar.'
Effie Loomis secretary from 1901; Teague bookkeeper 1905-1945; Sill buttermaker at Larrow Green, all inside Section A.
Section A gives Selby Vose as manager from 1913 but never says he was Gideon's son; the son relation appears only in B3 and cannot travel into A.
Story 6: yearly station-gain line from 1898, 'five and a quarter per cent, as usual', carried to the general account.
Ostrey Hollow skimming station, seven miles up, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed from Larrow Green.
Milk weighed, sampled, Babcock-tested, cream to Larrow Green and skim returned; the charge and the bottle 'ruled for the full charge' are in story 8. Core fact present.
Ammon & Sons, Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897; 1898 rejected.
Invoice table: 6 dozen pipettes marked 17.6, 12 dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, $77.93.
'The shortfall was 0.19 of a point and flat: the same in February as in July.'
'The pipette is the one instrument a tester cannot check at the bench', with Strawn first issued burettes in 1921. Credited with some hesitation, since 'none in the county' is left implicit.
Keddie born 1861, twenty-nine seasons 1896-1924, dismissed 30 April 1925, died 1934.
The test book is named and described (begun 4 May 1896, kept through 1924); the bolded gate is only 'test book'.
Both figures are in Section A: 1896 at 3.80 on borrowed glass and a station average of 3.61.
8 May-10 July 1911, nine weeks, 3.80 then back to 3.61, question mark.
Orra Brant, Emmet's younger sister, married Ansel; ties him to the largest loser.
1919 water circular signed by Vose; Keddie's 17 March statement that he never took cream and could not say why.
Died February 1934; test book to the Historical Rooms in 1959.
Hessel Bottom, six farms, Emmet Brant the largest.
Weigh book from 1 January 1897; the two columns always agreed.

Conflates the two gaps: calls 3.80 'the Larrow Green figure' (story 4) and 'the Larrow Green level' (D1), and at E8 rejects Roy's 0.17 in favour of 0.19 as 'the gap'. The key's gate says this loses the item.
Grigg committee, January-March 1908, hay verdict reported as the committee's finding, not as fact.
200,000 lb at a recorded 3.42; proportional error, 3.42 herd 0.18 short and 4.56 herd 0.24 short.
Roy from 1929, lent to Ivy 1958, Hazel from 1962.
Jerome Cudd, Alder Corners, Vessey County, over Redlow Ridge; 1914 opening kept with 1913 as the build year (inference); year does not gate.
From 1915 four of the six hauled over the ridge in the summer flush.
Other county (Vessey), own new glassware, never compared figures, a factory where Keddie had no hand.
Station figures for the same men 'ran about 0.19 lower until the glass was replaced'; sixteen seasons 1915-1930 stated.
'The same cows, on the same wet ground, in the same summers, tested 3.80' elsewhere; removes the land; cheese exposes watering.
Rosalie is Jerome's daughter (niece rejected) and copied the figures for Ivy in 1958.
Strawn, Ordell circuit 1907-1936, kin to nobody.
Section A says only that Strawn found no water in 1919. It never says he ran the lactometer on every visit and never once found water; that appears only in F.
12 June 1923, against his burette, condemned the whole crate.
Quotes 'I did not weigh what it has cost them'; gives no figure.

Ordered 28 June, Ammon reply 2 July, new glass in use July 1923, 1924 average 3.80 (3.90/3.85 rejected). Core fact present; the 'nobody connected it' clause is only implied by 'the crate was never mentioned'.
Crate to the loft; notebooks to the state dairy office, then the Farland library in 1947, where Ivy found the 1923 volume.
Petition January 1925.
Frick board, 17 March-4 May 1925; second and third sessions in the weigh room.
Water (Vose), cream-taking (Teague), 1908 hay report; none accepted.
Four books listed, including Strawn's 1923 notebook, but Section A never says the notebook held the answer and was read for its other lines; that point appears only in F.
Dismissed 30 April 1925 with no explanation accepted; 4 May award of $3,800 'without admission', charged to the station account; $3,500 rejected.
Gives the one fifth and 'charged to the station account' but never identifies it as the account into which the loss had built up as 'gain'. Section A even sends the gain to 'the general account'.
Ivy born 1931, Ansel's granddaughter, graduate student at Farland; Vaught named as her co-author on the bulletin.
'Put five records side by side': test book, weigh book, Alder Corners figures, Strawn notebooks, ledgers.
February 1958, station loft, nine pipettes.
9 March 1958, burette, 16.72 against 17.6, 0.88 short, 0.95.
Reads low in proportion: 3.80 read as 3.61, 0.19 short; the herd examples show it is proportional, not constant; span dates in A.
40,000,000 lb over 1898-1922, 76,000 lb, $19,000 at 25c; ledger totals give gain 76,000 lb.
Bulletin 471, October 1958; 35 years from condemnation, 33 since dismissal, died 1934.
Granddaughter.
Derived via Duncan; great-niece rejected.
Second cousins, with the correct derivation.

Correctly declines full vs half siblings (no deduction), but says instead that half siblings would make them 'half second cousins'. That contradicts the required statement that the doubt does not change the answer.
Gideon Vose, father; nephew rejected.
Son of the man who wrote Article VII, which made the station test final.
Headline 'none is established, and it cannot be proved either way'. It leans against kinship while declining to decide, so it is an abstention.
Two narrators from valley talk, one family denial that rests on negative evidence, no line of descent named, pre-1889 papers lost.
0.95, 5% low, one part in twenty.
5.26% of fat credited and 5.00% of fat delivered, denominators named.
$77.93 by summation.
72 pipettes, 0.88 c.c. each.
1 May 1897-12 June 1923 = 26 years 1 month 11 days (accepted form); 25 full years 1898-1922; part-year reason given.
Cannot be determined; both figures are hearsay and no record exists.
Variable: the measuring glass, the station's own pipette replaced by a borrowed measure.
Tester, bottles, acid, hand tester, scales, herds, pasture held constant.
3.80 through the nine weeks, back to 3.61 when the station's glass returned.
Rules out tester, hay, water and season; limits: size of the shortfall, whether every piece was short, whose measure was borrowed.
Ledger surplus (Teague/Kyle/Sill), 1911 (Keddie/Orra/Duncan), Alder Corners (Rosalie Cudd), 1924 (Strawn).
Independence argued; says reasons 1-4 hold without the 1958 measurement.
A09: headline verdict 'No.' In Section A it states as fact that Teague raised the matter with Vose in 1916. That is an assertion, so −2.
Yes, he knew the station ran low against the valley: 1902 complaints, 1919 circular.
Manager from 1913, signed ledger sheets with the gain line, wrote the 1919 circular.

A03: no verdict sentence, so no deduction. But 'no evidence that he knew' is not a declaration that the question cannot be settled, and it leans on Kyle's word as fact. Only one of the required observations (signature vs reading) is roughly present.
E.g. row 3 1924 average 3.80 by arithmetic; row 6 six farms by majority; row 5 weigh book 1897 by document; row 2 Jan-Mar sampling; row 7 Orra 1866.
Explicit list of two-narrator wrong values with breakers: 16.27 (NT-1), 12 July (NT-11), $77.39 (NT-14), 5.26% of actual fat (NT-20), etc.
A10 (E3) and A06 (E18) declined, each with what is established. A04 is declined only in Section A, not in B-G.
Self-refutations identified: r15, r18, r20, r05, r11 and others.
16.72/17.6, 95%, proportional error, onset 1897 with 1896 at 3.80, end 12 June 1923 with 1924 at 3.80, nothing on the farms changed.
Watering (Vose, Sill) defeated by Strawn's lactometer and Alder Corners 3.80.
Theft (Teague) defeated: the cream arrived heavy; 1911 and 1924 under the same tester.
Bog hay (Grigg, Kepp) defeated: Bulletin 214 found 0.05 in winter and nothing in summer, against a flat 0.19.
A07: 'Did the 1925 board examine the condemned glassware? No.' A headline verdict, so −2.
A05: 'What the tester believed: that it was the glass'. A headline verdict (also E45 'weight to the glass'), so −2.
About 143 words.
Ledger, Brant weigh book, Alder Corners tests, inspector's 1923 condemnation (Strawn notebook), 1958 crate/measurement, plus 1911 test-book entries.
Decoys given as what the Association blamed, not as fact; no wrong headline figures.

deductions.reason: Gullibility A09: asserts the bookkeeper's questioning (D2 'No.'; Section A states Teague raised it with Vose in 1916 as fact)
Gullibility A07: asserts the 1925 board did not examine the condemned glassware ('No.')
Gullibility A05: asserts what the tester believed ('that it was the glass')
